tasks.task: Write a one-page capability statement

items.when: When a firm needs one page on what it does, why choose it and past work, from its records
When the why-choose-us lines are flat, to see the value said several ways
When the buyer prefers a letter, to try the same capability as a short pitch letter
Before it goes out, to find every claim with no fact behind it and rewrite it
When the firm has supplied evidence, to see which claims go further than it allows
When the page is laid out, to read it as a facilities buyer with two minutes to spare

tasks.task: Write an intro email sequence to target buyers

items.when: When you want a short sequence to facilities, property or office managers
When the buyer is another kind of business and you need emails, follow-ups and a send setup
When one account matters, to get an email, a call script and a message from real signals
When the first line sounds like a pitch, to try an opener a stranger would answer
When the email is written and needs subject lines from several angles
Before sending, to test each claim, check the legal basics and tighten the email
When emails go out in batches and each batch should learn from the last one's replies

tasks.task: Write briefs and plans for target accounts

items.when: When a target account needs a brief and a plan from public pages and the client's notes
When you know only the company name and need a sourced file on it
When the account is known and needs goals, key people, risks and next steps written
When the account is large and buyer roles and deal risks need mapping in one run
When the plan names one contact, to map who else decides and who is missing
Before the brief is used in outreach, to date and source each fact about the account

tasks.task: Build a supplier pre-qualification pack and gap list

items.when: When the firm needs its policies, insurances and references gathered into one pack
When a buyer has sent the list of documents a supplier must provide
When the buyer sent a questionnaire, to sort must-haves and draft the answers
When a UK buyer asks for Cyber Essentials and the firm has not applied yet

tasks.task: Prepare a first meeting or site walk

items.when: When a commercial buyer has agreed to meet and you need questions and what to measure
When you need the order of questions from their situation to what a fix is worth
When the buyer shrugs at the problem, to ask what it costs them each month
When there were earlier calls, to get a one-page plan built on the last notes
When the plan is a presentation and should be questions about their problem

tasks.task: Turn a site walk into a quote scope and proposal

items.when: When visit notes must become an accurate scope with what is in and out
When you have call notes and photos and need a costed quote in the firm's template
When the proposal needs a margin check and a dated plan to signature
When the buyer could take a small start or a full contract, to price both shapes
Before it is sent, to read the quote as the buyer and list what they would have to ask

tasks.task: Review a live deal with MEDDICC

items.when: When a deal has gone quiet or its close date keeps slipping
When the review must update the account plan with the gaps found
When you want a health score, ranked risks and next actions for one deal
When the buyer likes you but will not decide, to find the doubt behind the delay
When the deal is silent, to get a firm recommendation and the follow-up to send
When the deal is stuck on fear of a wrong choice, not on preference for a rival

tasks.task: Build a target account list

items.when: When the firm is moving to a new kind of customer and the list is step one
When you can describe the ideal customer and need accounts with a reason for each
When the list needs contacts and company details added from many sources
When the list is long, to score fit and activity and sort it into tiers

tasks.task: Plan a new commercial accounts campaign

items.when: When a firm decides to win a new kind of customer or the pipeline has run dry
When outreach must become a repeatable weekly process with roles and a lead flow
When the budget could go to outreach or to partners, to see both plans with dates
Before the campaign starts, to name why it could fail in six months

tasks.task: Plan and write a partnership proposal

items.when: When the route is a referral partner, a joint bid, subcontracting or co-marketing
Before writing, to set partner types, incentives and how shared revenue is tested
When you have no partner in mind, to get several partner ideas and a joint plan
When the partnership should start as one small test with costs and decision rules
When terms are open, to find what a win is for each side and write the agreement
When a partner has approached the firm, to get a sign or pass call and terms to ask for

tasks.task: Write a first approach to a potential partner

items.when: When a partner is picked and needs a short first email with a reason to reply
When you have never met them, to try an opener built on what they care about
Before sending, to test each claim about the partner and tighten the email
When the email asks for a favour and offers the partner nothing first

tasks.task: Plan the route onto an approved supplier list

items.when: When a target buyer only buys from an approved list or a framework
When the list's entry rules are known and the firm's documents must be checked against them
When you need to find open bids worth chasing and a go or no-go on each
When the firm could apply alone or under a partner, to compare both routes with dates

tasks.task: Answer a tender or RFP question set

items.when: When the tender arrives, to sort requirements by must-have and score the fit
Before drafting, to choose win themes and a one-page summary to build around
When the answers need value, price, timeline and proof for this buyer
Before submission, to remove every bid claim that has no fact behind it

tasks.task: Plan cold calls and LinkedIn approaches

items.when: When the buyer answers the phone and you need an opener, questions and brush-off replies
When you want three short, honest opening questions to try on the first calls
When the buyers are on LinkedIn and you need who to follow, notes and a plan
When asked what the firm does, to have 10, 30 and 60 second answers ready
When you have two or three openers, to let a fresh reviewer pick one as the buyer

tasks.task: Prepare a negotiation on price and terms

items.when: When terms are on the table and you need an opening, questions and a fallback
When the buyer holds the power, to set your terms, their needs and the order to move
When the buyer sends their contract, to flag risky terms before a lawyer sees it
When the buyer says the price is too high and you are about to offer a discount

tasks.task: Answer objections and comparisons with the incumbent

items.when: When the buyer has said something specific, to see what it means and how to reply
When one rival holds the contract, to prepare comparisons and reply scripts
Before a comparison is sent, to check each point against a fact the firm can show

tasks.task: Follow up a meeting and keep the deal moving

items.when: When you have notes from the meeting and need a follow-up email and CRM updates
When the buyer is keen, to share a dated plan of steps on both sides to signature
When emails, calls and meetings must be written back to the deal record
Before the follow-up goes, to check it promises only what was agreed in the room

tasks.task: Turn past work into case studies and proof

items.when: When a happy client has never been asked, to send a short request with three questions
When you have one client interview and need a case outline and its evidence gaps
When account notes must become a leave-behind with no made-up numbers
Before a case study is used, to check each result against the client's records

tasks.task: Review the pipeline and forecast

items.when: Each week, to see what changed and which deals to act on today
When you have deals and a target, to check cover and how accurate the forecast is
When the numbers look off, to list missing fields, stale dates and wrong stages

tasks.task: Find why deals are won and lost

items.when: When you have notes on won and lost deals and want the real reason you win
When closed deals sit in the CRM and you need loss stages and common objections
Each month, to turn last month's losses into a revised pitch

tasks.task: Work a trade event and follow up the contacts

items.when: Before the event, to prepare short answers and an opening question
After the event, to group contacts by what each asked for and draft the follow-ups
Before the follow-ups go, to check each one refers to what was really said

always.when: Before any statement, bid or email leaves, to tie each fact to the firm's own records
Before anything goes to a buyer, to catch typos and a buyer's name spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the opening turns into a full tender or a long written bid
When outreach must run daily at volume, not as one sequence
When the quote needs a pricing model for a recurring contract, not a single price
When the pack lacks policies, certificates or insurance the buyer requires
When the firm must first choose which sector or region to enter
When the capability statement needs a designed layout for print or PDF

gaps: No library item writes a one-page capability statement; the nearest writes a pitch letter
No library item builds a pre-qualification pack or checks a firm against a buyer's document list
No library item covers supplier accreditation schemes such as SafeContractor, CHAS or Constructionline
No library item prepares a site walk question sheet or turns site measurements into a quote scope
No library item writes a teaming, joint bid or subcontract proposal to a larger prime
No library item runs a MEDDICC review as its main job
No library item prices a recurring service contract from hours, sites and margin
No library item plans how to displace an incumbent supplier, including the switch-over plan
No library item finds frameworks and approved lists for a small firm's trade and region
No library item offers clearly different capability statement layouts to compare
